title: Projects a machine wants the fleet to infer
description: A machine whose admitted memory cannot infer the stale projects of a graph read publishes this request instead of computing them; a machine with headroom serves it by inferring the projects, whose records reach the requester through the project record exchange. The Policy numbers are measured: the parent holds 7.1 GB in one wave of 48 projects (7 121 MB, 7 172 MB) and 1.0 to 2.1 GB while it only verifies.

ServeState.description: What the graph server of a machine keeps in serve-state.json between two of its processes: the requests it holds with the projects it already reported fresh, the claim keys it completed (at most 4096, the newest) and the kind of read that was running. A new process of the same owner and platform renews the claims, answers with at least these projects and tells its read which projects are published already.

ReadStop.description: EN: why the server stopped a graph read, written to read-stop.json BEFORE the signal is sent: the verdict, the milliseconds without progress, the newest generation and each phase or owner ledger's highest completed count with its reported total. DE: warum der Server ein Graph-Lesen beendet hat, vor dem Signal in read-stop.json geschrieben: Urteil, Millisekunden ohne Fortschritt, neueste Generation und der höchste Fertigzähler jeder Phase oder Projektbilanz samt gemeldeter Gesamtzahl.

ReadRecord.description: What the detached runner of a graph read keeps in read-record.json, replaced atomically every beat: the kind of read, the pid of the runner and of the read, when the read started, when the runner last wrote, the log file with the progress output of the read and, once the read ended, its exit status and the time. A process of the graph server that finds a record whose runner lives and beat lately attaches to the read instead of starting another; a record with a status is the result of a read that ended while no server watched.

ReadWatchCheckpoint.description: Local handoff of a graph read watchdog at a complete log line.
